```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets) # Using the data sets package
library(plotly)
library(lubridate) # For data cleaning
library(viridis) # Used for Plot 3
```

```{r data}
# Loading data set of choice:

data("rest_inspec")

# We can go ahead and clean our data set:

rest_inspec_clean =
  rest_inspec %>% 
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(
    cuisine_description = case_match(
      # Simplifying one of the cuisine labels so reads better in plot
      cuisine_description,
      "Latin (Cuban, Dominican, Puerto Rican, South & Central American)" ~ "Latin (Non-Mexican)",
      .default = cuisine_description # Keeping all other cuisine labels as they are
    )) %>% 
  # Kept getting some weird latitude and longitudes when making first plot, so filtering for that here:
  filter(
    latitude != 0, longitude != 0, !is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude),
    
    # Removing a single extreme outlier from Queens o 164. Keeping the NAs for now (they are removed later)
    
    is.na(score) | score < 164
  )

```


Column {data-width=600}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Scatterplot: Average Restaurant Inspection Score by NYC Geolocation in Manhattan

```{r scatterplot}
# For the first plot, I will create a geographical scatter plot detailing the average inspection score for distinct locations:

rest_inspec_clean %>% 
  distinct( # Making sure we have distinct observations to avoid repeats
    latitude, longitude, camis, dba, boro, inspection_date, score
  ) %>% 
  group_by(latitude, longitude, camis, dba, boro) %>% # Grouping to avoid repeats
  summarize(
    avg_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE) # Creating the average score across locations
  ) %>% 
  mutate( # Creating labels for the hover menu
    text_label = str_c(
      "Average Score: ", round(avg_score, 2), # Rounding the average
      "<br>Restaurant Name: ", dba,
      "<br>NYC Borough: ", boro) # notice the added line break
  ) %>% 
  filter( # Removing missing values for the coordinates and mean score
    boro == "Manhattan", # Decided to simplify and keep it to Manhattan data
    !is.na(latitude),
    !is.na(longitude),
    !is.na(avg_score)
  ) %>% 
  plot_ly(
    x = ~longitude, y = ~latitude, type = "scatter", mode = "markers", 
    color = ~avg_score, text = ~text_label, alpha = 0.5,
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) %>% 
  layout(
    title = "Average Inspection Score by Restaurant in Manhattan",
    xaxis = list(title = "Longitude"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Latitude"),
    #Checked how to add legend on StackOverflow:
    annotations = list(list(
      text = "NOTE: Lower inspection scores indicate better performance.",
      xref = "paper",
      yref = "paper",
      x = 0.02, # This adds positioning coordinates
      y = 0.98,
      showarrow = FALSE, # This keeps as plain text
      xanchor = "left",
      yanchor = "top"
  ))) %>%  # Adding space below the graph for the legend
  # Changing the label of the legend
  colorbar(title = "Average\nInspection\nScore")
```

### Boxplot: Average Inspection Score by Top 10 Cuisines in NYC: Brooklyn vs. Queens

```{r boxplot}
# Created code separately to identify the top 10 cuisines from the inspection data:

top10 =
  rest_inspec_clean %>% 
  distinct(cuisine_description, camis) %>% # Finding by distinct cuisine and rest
  count(cuisine_description, sort=TRUE) %>%  # Getting the sorted counts
  slice_head(n=10) %>% 
  pull(cuisine_description)

# Now doing my boxplot only with the Top 10 cuisines to make it less messy:

rest_inspec_clean %>%
  distinct( # Making sure inspection scores are not repeated from different instances of violations
    cuisine_description, camis, dba, boro, inspection_date, score
  ) %>%
  filter(
    cuisine_description %in% top10, # Filtering for only Top 10 cuisines
    # I kept getting a boro group equal to zero, so I removed that:
    boro != "0",
    # Decided to simplify and do a Brooklyn vs. Queens comparison:
    boro %in% c("Brooklyn", "Queens")
  ) %>%
  group_by(cuisine_description, camis, dba, boro) %>% # Grouping by camis which represents a unique restaurant
  summarize(
    avg_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE) # Getting the average score
  ) %>% 
  filter( # Removing the NA values
    !is.na(avg_score),
    !is.na(cuisine_description)
  ) %>%
  mutate( # Adding labels and reordering like in lecture
    cuisine_label = str_to_title(cuisine_description), # Cleaning my title
    cuisine_label = fct_reorder(cuisine_label, avg_score) # Ordering
  ) %>% 
  plot_ly(
    x = ~cuisine_label, y = ~avg_score, color = ~boro, type = "box",
    line = list(color = "black"),# Making the boxplot outline black
    marker = list(size = 6, opacity = 0.7) # Changing size and transparency of points in the box plot
  ) %>% 
  layout(
    title = "Average Inspection Score by Top 10 Cuisines: Brooklyn vs. Queens",
    xaxis = list(title = "Cuisine", automargin = TRUE,# Adding margin since long label
                 tickfont = list(size = 10)), 
    yaxis = list(title = "Average Inspection Score"),
    boxmode = "group", # Putting boxes side by side
    
    # Had to add even more code to make sure the legend satayed in place:
    legend = list(  # Legends will be side by side
    orientation = "h", x = 0.5, xanchor = "center", y = -0.32, yanchor = "top"),
    
    # Checked on StackOverflow how to add a legend:
    annotations = list(list(
      text = "NOTE: Lower inspection scores indicate better performance.",
      xref = "paper",
      yref = "paper",
      x = 0.5, # This adds positioning coordinates
      y = 0.92,
      showarrow = FALSE, # This keeps as plain text
      xanchor = "center",
      yanchor = "top"
    )))
```

### Barchart: Restaurant Inspection Grades by NYC Borough

```{r barchart}

rest_inspec_clean %>%
  distinct( # Making sure inspection grades are not repeated
    grade, camis, dba, boro, inspection_date
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(grade),!is.na(boro)
  ) %>%
  # Following the example from lecture:
  count(grade, boro) %>% # Counting the inspection by grade and boro
  plot_ly(
    x = ~boro, y = ~n, color = ~grade, type = "bar", 
    colors = viridisLite::viridis(7) # Kept running into issues with viridis so had to specify
  ) %>% 
  layout(
    title = "Restaurant Inspection Grades by Borough in NYC",
    xaxis = list(title = "Borough"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Number of Inspections"),
    barmode = "group" # This allows me to compare grade grouping bars per boro
  )

```
